sections.text: # The Superhero Tradition: Golden to Modern Age

metadata.title: The Superhero Tradition: Golden to Modern Age
The Superhero Tradition: Golden to Modern Age

sections.text:
```
+------------------------------------------------------------------+
|               AMERICAN SUPERHERO COMICS AGES                     |
|                                                                  |
|  GOLDEN AGE (1938-1956)                                          |
|  Superman (1938), Batman (1939), Wonder Woman (1941)             |
|  WWII propaganda; crime-fighting; wish fulfillment               |
|  Comics Code Authority (1954) ends the age                       |
|                                                                  |
|  SILVER AGE (1956-1970)                                          |
|  DC revamp; Marvel revolution (Stan Lee/Jack Kirby/Steve Ditko)  |
|  Spider-Man (1962), X-Men (1963), Fantastic Four (1961)          |
|  Characters with flaws; teenage heroes; existential doubt        |
|                                                                  |
|  BRONZE AGE (1970-1985)                                          |
|  Darker stories; Green Lantern/Green Arrow; drug PSA arc         |
|  X-Men revival (Claremont/Byrne); Daredevil (Miller)             |
|                                                                  |
|  MODERN AGE (1986-2000)                                          |
|  Watchmen, Dark Knight: deconstruction; adult content            |
|  Vertigo imprint (DC, 1993); Image Comics (1992)                 |
|                                                                  |
|  CONTEMPORARY (2000-present)                                     |
|  MCU adaptation dominates; Ultimate line; events + crossovers    |
+------------------------------------------------------------------+
```
